full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the respondents filed the aforesaid suit seeking declaration of their title to 1.84 acres of land. (They added the prayer for partition in the revisional stage) stating, inter alia, that the land appertaining to R.S. Khatin No. 21 measuring an area of 12.95 acres along with other lands originally belonged to Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu, Rajmohon got 4.27 acres of land in his share and after his death, his 8 sons Kailash, Rasik, Rojoni, Surjokanto, Rakhal, Piyari and Choto incherited his share. Ketu, while residing with his brother Rajmohon, executed a Will on 17.02.1913 in favour of his nephew Kailash to the extent of 12 annas and to his wife Feli to the extent of 4 annas share specifically pointing out that on her demise Kailash would get his entire share. Accordingly, after the death of Feli, Kailash got Ketu's share to the extent of 4.27 acres of land by virtue of the said Will. He also inherited a share as son of Rajmohan. Jogesh Chandra, being only son of Kailash, inherited the entire share left by Kailash but in the R.S. Khatian only 4 annas share was recorded in his name though he acquired 6 annas share out of the total land. Panchu died leaving two sons, Kanai Lal and Kalicharan @ Khoka but in the R.S. and S.A. Khatians more shares were recorded in their names. Jogesh Chandra transferred 1.34 acres of land out of his 4.86 acres, by registered kabala dated 19th August 1957, in favour of the plaintiff No. 1, his mother Maloti and the plaintiff No. 4. On the same day, Jogesh, by another deed, transferred 1.34 acres of land in favour of Kishore, Mohananda and Satish, the predecessor's of the plaintiffs. Kalicharan @ Khoka, by a registered dated 2nd June 1958 exchanged .84 acre of land with Mohananda, Kishore and Satish. Pursuant to that exchange deed, Kishore, Mohananda and Satish got lands of Shakhari Kati Mouja and Kalicharan got lands of the Gaokhali Mouja. Mohananda died leaving on issue and, accordingly, Kishore inherited his share and on the death of Kishore, the plaintiffs got his share. Satish, died without any issue and, accordingly, the plaintiffs got his share. Thus, the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree to the extent of 1.84 acres of land. 

 3. The defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending that in the suit khatian Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu had 13.13 acres of land and, accordingly, each brother got 4.38 acres. Rajmohon died leaving behind 8 sons and each son inherited .49½ acre of land. Ketu died leaving without any issue and, therefore, his brother Panchu inherited his share. Thus, Panchu got 8.75 acres of land. Out of 13.13 acres of land, Rajmohon, Panchu and Ketu settled 1.16 acres to different tenants. Panchu, in fact, got 7.86 acres of land after the settlement. After his death, Kanai and Kalicharan, his two sons, inherited the same. Kanai died leaving 4 sons Judhusthir, Nittynnanda, Gouranga and Narayan, who transferred 3.93 acres of land in favour of defendant No.3 by executing 5 sale deeds. The sale deeds and deed of exchange as mentioned in the plaint by the plaintiffs were forged and collusive and they did not acquire any title to the said lands on the basis of those deeds. 

 9. It was the case of the plaintiffs that the land measuring an area of 12.83 acres of R.S.Khatian No.21 originally belonged to Rajmohan, Ketu and Panchu. Each brother got 4.27 acres of land in their respective shares. Rajmohan died leaving 8 sons Kailash, Rashik, Rojoni, Surjokanto, Rakhal, Piyari and Choto. It was the further case of the plaintiffs that Ketu, having had no issue, executed a Will on 17.02.1913 in favour of Kailash to the extent of 12 annas and to his wife Feli to the extent of 4 annas share out of his share. There was a stipulation in the said Will that after the death of Feli, her interest would be devolved upon Kailash by virtue of the Will. Accordingly, after the death of Feli, Kailash got entire 'Ard share of Ketu, that is, to the extent of 4.27 acres of land. It was the claim of the plaintiffs that Kailash, by virtue of the Will and as son of Rajmohon, acquired 4.86 acres of land. Thereafter, Kailash died leaving only son Jogesh Chandra as his heir. Panchu died leaving behind two sons Kanai and Kalicharan. Jogesh sold 1.34 acres to the plaintiffs on 19.08.1957. He again sold 1.34 acres of land to Kishore, Mohananda and Satish, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by another deed dated 19.08.1957. Kalicharan exchanged his .84 acre of land with Kishore, Mohananda and Satish by a deed of exchange dated 02.06.1958. Mohananda died without issue and his share was devolved to Kishore. Satish died leaving plaintiffs No.1-3 as his heirs. 

 16. The plaintiffs in their plaint initially stated that the land measuring an area of 12.95 acres appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.21 and Plots Nos.2208, 2209, 2210, 2211, 2212, 2213, 2214, 2215, 2216, 2219, 2221 and 2280 of Gowkhali Mouza belonged to Kailash, Harihor, Kiron Chanda, Rajanikanta, Kartick, Brata Beway, Fulmala, Koti Sundari, Kanai Lal and Kalicharan in their respective shares in different groups. It was their further case that those lands were recorded in S.A. Khatian Nos.39,213,217,311 and 194. From S.A. Khatians ext.3 series it appears that the land measuring an area of 7.96 acres of plots Nos.2209, 2210, 2211, 2212 and 2213 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.39 was recorded in the names of Kanai Lal and Kali Charan. The land measuring an area of .70 acre of Plot No.2208 of S.A. Khatian No.213(Ext. 3 Ka) was recorded in the name of Jogesh Chandra son of Kailash Chandra Halder. The land measuring .92 acre of plots No.2215 and 2280 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.217 (Ext.3Kha) was recorded in the name of Rajani Kanta. The land measuring 1.74 acres of Plot Nos.2214, 2215, 2221, 2280 and 2220 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No.31 1(ext. 3Ga) was recorded in the names of Harihor and Keron Chandra and the land measuring an area of .95 of Plots No.2215, 2216 and 2219 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 154 (ext.3 gha) was recorded in the name of Brata Bewa. From Ext.1 (R.S. Khatian No.21) it appears that name of Kailash, father of Jogesh, was recorded to the extent of 4' annas share but in remarks column, which is the column regarding the name of the possessor, his name was mentioned against plot No.2208 in respect of .70 acre of land only which was subsequently recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 213(ext.3Ka) in S.A. operation. In his cross examination P.W.1 has said "এস,এ, খতিয়ানে যোগেশের ৭০ শতক রেকর্ড হওয়া দৃষ্ট হয়।" Jogesh did not take any step to get the S.A. khatian corrected claiming more land by virtue of the disputed Will. 

 17. By way of amendment of the pleading, the plaintiffs added that the land measuring an area of 12.83 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.311 and Plots No.5794, 5495, 5496, 5497, 5498, 5501, 5502, 5503, 5504, 5505 and 5506 belonged Rajmohan, Katu and Panehu. Rajmohon having 4.27 acres of land died leaving 8 sons Kailash, Rashik, Rajani, Kartic, Surjakanta, Rakhal, Peari and Chuta. Katu, having had no issue, executed a Will in favour of brother's son Kailash and wife Fell on 17.02.1913 in respect of 12 annas and 4 annas shares respectively. That is, the said will was executed before C.S. operation. P.W.1 in his cross-examination has said, “আমার বয়স ৫০/৫২। ১৭-০২-১৯৩ ইং তারিখের দলিল সম্পর্কে আমার ব্যক্তিগত ধারনা নাই।” He further said, "সি, এস এ কেতুরামের নামে রেকর্ড আছে " From the pleadings, evidence mentioned above, C.S. khatian (ext. Ka), R.S. Khatian (ext.1) and S.A. Khatians (ext 3 series) it appear that those records were not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will (Ext 7). It is to be mentioned here that in the schedule of Will (ext.7) names and particulars of the properties Willed were not mentioned. Though Will was allegedly executed on 17.02.1913 and C.S. Khatian was prepared and published thereafter, the same was not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will rather the same was prepared and published in the names of Ketu (the alleged testator) and his two brothers Rajmohan and Panchu. C.S. Khatian has got presumptive value though rebutable. An entry in C.S. record-of-right is presumed to be correct until the contrary is shown. The C.S. record-of-right being prepared with considerable formality and the proceedings of Revenue Officers being conducted with publicity, the entries in such records should not be lightly discarded. From the preparation of C.S. Khatian in the name of Ketu, two things are clear which are (1) at the time preparation of Khatian Ketu was alive and (2) the same was not prepared in accordance with the terms of alleged Will. The plaintiffs did not take any step to rebut the presumption of C.S. Khatian. It appears from the transfer deed dated 29.8.1957 executed by Jogesh son of Kailash in favour of Kammakkhya and others (ext.4) and deed dated 29.8.1957 executed by said Jogesh to Kaishore Halder and others (ext.5) he did not recite that he had acquired title to the land transferred by virtue of the Will executed by Ketu to his father Kailash. After 85 years of alleged execution of Will the plaintiffs, for the first time, disclosed about the existence of the Will. The last Court of facts rightly drew conclusion that the Will is a suspicious document. The suspicion of the Court of facts has got basis because- (1) the plaintiffs disclosed about the Will after 85 years of its execution; (2) No evidence has been adduced in respect of its execution, attestation and recitation to the testator; (3) No date of death of the testator has been mentioned in the pleadings or in evidence to decide the issue whether probate of the Will was mandatory or not; (4) C.S., R.S. and S.A. khatians were not prepared fol-lowing the terms of the Will; (5) In the recital of sale deeds of '1957 there were no recitation that Jogesh acquired title to 4.86 acres of land from his father Kailash, who got the same on the basis of Will and (6) Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor paid any rent of the suit land since last 85 years. 

 18. In the case of Ram Copal V. Alpana Kumer reported in AIR 1922 P.C. 366 Judicial Committee of the Privy Council observed that a Will is one of the most solemn documents known to the law. By it a dead man entrusts to the living, the carrying out of his wishes, and it is impossible that he can be called either to deny signature or to explain the circumstances in which it was executed it is essential that trustworthy and effective evidence should be given to establish compliance with the necessary forms of law. The High Court Division accepted the Will simply for the reason that the same was 30 years old document and as such it is to be presumed genuine. But the presumption under Section 90 of the Evidence Act can be drawn in the case of Wills, the genuineness of which is in controversy in the Probate case. Execution and attestation of a Will more than thirty years old and produced from proper custody may be presumed to be true. But where the propounder of the Will has not made any averment in the pleadings that the Will was acted upon after the death of the testator and the testator was in sound disposition of mind at the time of execution, and that the Will was duly attested and it was the last Will of the testator, the presumption under Section 90 of the Evidence Act cannot be extended to a Will even if it was/is a registered Will. Within the four corners of the plaint we did not find any such averment. Since the testator, by the alleged Will bequeathed all his property to his one nephew excluding his heirs; the court has to scrutinize the evidence in support of the execution of the Will with a greater degree of care than usual Non-production of Will anywhere since last 85 years creates suspicion and it was the duty of the plaintiffs to remove all such suspicions. But P.W.1 who exhibited the Will (ext.7), in his evidence, has said, “১৭-০২-১৯১৩ ইং তারিখের দলিল সম্পর্কে আমার ব্যক্তিগত ধারনা নেই।” He was the only witness who said about the Will. 

 19. The High Court Division in its judgment has given much importance on the point that since will was executed before enforcement of the Succession Act, 1925 it was not required to be probated. It is the settled principle that the declaration made in the Will should be operative after the death of the testator and not before that. In this case, we do not find anything either in the plaint or in the evidence as to the date of death of the testator Ketu which was relevant for the decision whether probate of the instant Will was mandatory or not. We have already found from the admission of P.W.1 that C.S. Khatian was prepared in the name of Ketu (not in the name of Kailash) which indicates that Ketu was alive at the time of preparation of C.S. Khatian. So, it is difficult to say that at the time of enforcement of the Succession Act in 1925 Ketu was not alive. In the case of Hem Nolini Vs. Isolyne Sarojbashini reported in AIR 1962 SC 1471 subject matters were three Wills. One was of April 1921, second one was of June 1925 and third one was of April 1930. No probates of the first and second Will were taken out. Testator died in 1934. In such circumstances Supreme Court of India observed that no person can claim as a legatee or as an executor unless he obtains probate or letters of administration of the Will under which he claims. 

 21. Since C.S. and R.S. and S.A. Khatians were not prepared and published in accordance with the terms of the Will and the same came into light after 85 years of its execution and no evidence was led to prove the Will to satisfy the conscience of the Court that it was the last Will of a free and capable testator so, it is difficult to accept that the Will has been duly proved. Moreover, the last Court of facts, considering the evidence, held that the Will has not been acted upon. Since the requirements of law is that the Will should be attested by two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the testator to sign and should sign the Will in the presence of the testator, the Court while examining the question as the Will propounded has been duly executed by the testator of the Will, whether the same suffers from suspicious circumstances and it is the last Will and testament of the testator, Will have to be care-fully analysed upon examining the evidence adduced before the Court. In this case, the revisional Court reversed the finding of facts arrived at by the last Court of facts ignoring the above requirements of law.

lawyer:
AB Roy Chowdhury, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
AQ Rashid Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General -----For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property (now vested property), Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 34 of 1970 for declaration of title in the suit property and for a further declaration that the suit property cannot be treated as Enemy property (Vested property). The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that, Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu is the owner of the property and it has been rightly recorded as such in CS Khatian Nos. 68 and 142 of Mouza Kirtibashdi under police station Raipura in the District of Dhaka as a rent-free debutter property of Bigraha Narayan Jeu and the plaintiff Narayan Jeu has been owning and possessing' the same although without any interruption. It has also been alleged that during the SA operation the suit property was wrongly recorded in the name of one Suresh Chandra. Roy, who had no right, title interest and possession therein at any point of time and there is absolutely no basis for the fraudulent entry in the SA Khatian. It has also been alleged that recently defendants 1 and 2 made illegal exercises for treating the suit property as an enemy property, now vested property, taking advantage of the wrong SA Khatian and this necessitated the filing of the suit. It has also been alleged that it was on 12-5-69 the plaintiff for the first time learnt that the suit property has been enlisted by the defendants as a vested property. 

 7. Mr. AB Roy Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Courts below evidently erred in law in dismissing the suit without admitting and considering the evidence of any of the eight witnesses examined by the contending parties and on misconstruction of CS Khatian Ext. 1 and 1(a) and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in the face of the consistent and overwhelming evidence proving that the plaintiff Deity is the owner of the suit property and the suit property is a deb utter property and the deity has been in physical existence in the suit property all through, the learned Court of appeal below evidently erred in law, on misreading and non-reading on the materials evidence and on mere surmises, to hold that the Deity migrated to India following which the suit property has become an enemy property and subsequently vested property and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in the face of the CS khatian Exts.1 and 1(a) clearly showing the suit property as a rent free debutter property of Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and there being absolutely no evidence on record to prove as to how the suit property became the secular property of Suresh Chandra Roy, and the plaintiff being in continuous peaceful possession of the same all through, the learned Courts below erred in law in holding on mere surmises and conjectures that the suit property was the personal property of Suresh Chandra Roy and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate submits that in the face of the clear assertion in the plaint and in the face of clear evidence of PW 1 that for the first time on 12-5-1969 he learnt that the suit property was being treated as vested property by the defendants and that he never filed any objection in any abandoned property proceeding or vested property proceeding in connection with the suit property and there being even no suggestion by the contesting defendants to that effect, the learned Courts below were manifestly wrong in illegally finding that the plaintiff had earlier knowledge about treating the suit property as an abandoned property, as a result of which the suit is barred by limitation under section 92/(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 10. PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee stated in his evidence that he is the Shebait of the plaintiff Deity Sree Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and the suit land belongs to the plaintiff Deity. He also stated that the usufructs of the suit properties are used for the daily seva puja of the plaintiff and for holding periodical parvans of the Deity. He also stated that the properties belong to the Deity since time immemorial as debutter property. He added that before him his father Debendra was the Shehait and before him Sharat Chandra Bhattacharjee was the Shebait of the plaintiff. He also stated that in the CS Khatian Exts.1 and 1(a) the suit land has been recorded in the name of the plaintiff a debutter property. He further stated that the original Bigraha was installed in a mud-walled temple but this temple subsequently became dilapidated following which the Deity was installed in a thatched hut and a pucca building of the deity is already under construction. He further stated besides the plaintiff Deity there are other Deities in the suit premises for a long time and the plaintiff and the other Deities were never removed to any other place at any point of time. He also stated that he sees the plaintiff in possession of the suit property from his childhood. He stated that the suit property was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Chandra Roy, although he had no title interest and possession therein. He stated that he cultivated a portion of the suit property himself and his bargadars cultivated the remaining portion. He clearly stated that no notice was served upon the plaintiff or upon him for treating the suit property as enemy property. He also stated that he never heard earlier that the suit property had been declared as abandoned property. He asserted that the plaintiff was never dispossessed from the suit property. He clearly stated in his evidence that he did not file any objection in the Enemy property office or Abandoned property office in connection with the suit property. He sated that Naib of Harirobi Tahsil office took his signatures on some papers on the plea that he would get the debutter property released from the list of the enemy property. 

 17. In cross-examination he stated that he cannot say the plot No. and the Khatian No. of the land he cultivated as the bargardar of the plaintiff. 

 21. In cross-examination he stated that he is an auditor serving at Dhaka since 1967 and he lives in Dhaka. He admitted that he has no other paper except the SA Khatian to show that the suit property actually belonged to Chandra Roy. He denied the suggestion put by the plaintiff that they created false papers for illegally grabbing the suit property in collusion with some officials of the Revenue Department. He stated that he cannot say if pujas are held in the tin shed constructed by PW 1. 

 25. From the scrutiny of the evidence discussed above it is clearly seen that it has been established by most convincing and overwhelming evidence that Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha has been in physical existence in the suit premises from time immemorial and it never migrated to India at any point of time. It has also been proved by most cogent and consistent evidence that PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee has been the Shebait of the Deity since the death of his father Debendra Chandra Bhattacharjee and before him Suresh Chandra Chakrobarty was the Shebait of the Deity. CS khatians Exts. 1 to 1(a) clearly prove that one Suresh Chandra Roy was the Shebait of the Deity at the time of the preparation of the CS record and Deity Lakshmi Jeu Bigraha is the owner of the suit property as a rent free jote. It is thus evident that the learned Courts below on misreading and non- reading of the material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the CS Khatians Exts.1 and 1(a) found that it has not been proved that PW 1 Prafullah Chandra Bhattacharjee is the Shehait of the Deity. It has been proved by most consistent and overwhelming evidence that the plaintiff has been in actual physical possession of suit property all through and the usufructs of the suit property are used for the daily seba pujas of the Deity. The witnesses examined by the plaintiff are all independent, natural and probable witnesses and their evidence does not suffer from any legal infirmity. 

 26. On the other hand, the DWs are not only interested witnesses but also they do not appear even to know the suit property. In this case, no witness has been examined on behalf of the Government. DW 1 Aziz serves in the AC Office at Dhaka and he is the alleged lessee of, a portion of the suit property. He has practically no knowledge about the origin of the suit property. DW 2 Md Sirajuddin serves in the T&T Department at Dhaka and he is a co-villager of DW 1. He has practically no knowledge about the suit property. DW 3 Ramijuddin Ali serves in the T&T Department at Dhaka. He admitted in his evidence that he cannot say if there is any hut in the suit property. It is thus evident that the DWs have- no direct knowledge about the possession of the suit property. The contesting defendants miserably failed to prove by any reliable evidence that they actually obtained delivery of possession in the suit property on the basis of the alleged settlement from the Government. The defence has totally failed to prove by any evidence as to how the contesting defendants possess the suit land. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it must be held that the paper relied on by the contesting defendants in support of their claim are essentially paper transactions for creating a basis of claim in support of the defendants' case. In the face of the CS khatian which clearly show that the suit property is a rent-free debutter property belonging to Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu Bigraha and Suresh Chandra Roy was simply the Shebait of the deity at the relevant time, it is manifestly evident that the suit property belongs to the plaintiff Deity as a debutter property and it never belonged to Suresh Chandra Roy as his personal property. The SA khatian prepared in the name of Suresh Chandra Roy in thus found to be without any basis at all and consequently, it is of no legal consequence. The learned Courts below on mis-construction of the CS khatians Exts 1 and 1(a) took the suit property as the personal property of the Shebait of the plaintiff and fell in error in finding that the suit property, in course of time, became the secular property of Suresh Chandra Roy, on mere surmises and conjectures. These findings by the learned courts below are vitiated by misreading and non-reading of the materials evidence and misconstruction of CS khatians Exts 1 and 1(ka) has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. There is absolutely nothing on record to find that the Deity migrated to India at any point of time or that it was taken to India by the Shebait and consequently the finding of the learned Court of appeal below on this point is evidently against the evidence on record, simply being the product of wild imagination, which cannot be allowed to stand. Since the plaintiff has successfully proved that the suit property belongs to Deity Lakshmi Narayan Jeu Bigraha and the plaintiff has been in physical possession thereof all through, the illegal exercises made by the defendants to treat the suit property sometimes as an abandoned property and sometimes as a vested property are found to be patently illegal and malafide moves, having no sanction of law. 

 28. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below. seriously erred in law in dismissing the suit on non-reading and misreading of the material evidence on record and on misconstruction of the important documents in the CS Khatians Exts. 1 and 1(a) and the same has occasioned failure of justice. As the plaintiff has been able to prove its title in the suit land and continuous possession therein, I do not find any reason as to why the suit should not be decreed. In view of the fact that the suit property is a Debutter property of the Deity and there is absolutely no basis for its becoming the secular property of its former Shebait Suresh, the mere recording of the suit property in the name of Suresh in SA khatian is evidently wrong and without any foundation whatsoever and the same cannot affect the plaintiffs right, title and interest in the suit property and any way there is no dispute to the proposition that the CS khatians has a presumption of correctness undersection 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act while the SA khatian has no such presumptive value. The learned Courts below thus evidently erred in law in placing too much reliance on the SA khatians completely ignoring the overwhelming evidence on record to prove that it had no legal foundation and factual basis. For the reasons stated above, I am constrained to hold that the learned Courts below were wrong in passing the impugned judgments on erroneous view of law and on illegal and irrelevant considerations and the same are liable to be set aside in the interest of justice.

lawyer:
Naima Haider, with Ms Mubina Asaf Rahman, Advocates —For the Petitioners. 
Abul Kalam Azad, Advocate — For the Opposite Parties No.1-11.
parties:
Shamsul Alam and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Muslehuddin @ Md Muslem and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
4. Sur Ali, Muklesh, Musa Ali and their mother, Ali Bibi were the owners of the suit land and the record of right was prepared in their names. The plaintiff purchased the said land by way of two sale deeds dated 31-1-1946 and 18-5-1952 from the heirs of the said recorded owners. RS record was prepared in the name of Sur Ali and other owners. The plaintiff had no knowledge of the wrong record in the name of Sur Ali and others, The MRR Khatian had been also prepared in the name of Sur Ali and others and the said record is absolutely wrong. The suit land was sold in auction for arrears of rent due to the Government in a certificate case of the year 1960 and was purchased by the defendants. The certificate case was stated making the recorded owners Sur Ali and others as certificate debtors. The certificate proceeding is collusive, illegal, void and without jurisdiction. The certificate sale was not acted upon and the auction purchaser did not acquire any right, title and possession on the suit land and the right, title and interest of the plaintiff has not been affected by the auctions sale. The defendants, though purchased the suit land from the auction purchaser, got no title and possession there and the suit land is possessed by the plaintiff. The cause of the suit arose on 8th Aswin, 1387 BS when the defendants, in the event of plaintiff''s dispossession over the suit or a portion of the suit land by the defendants. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 5-7 entered appearance in the suit and contested the same by filing written statement traversing all the material allegations made in the plaint. It is the case of the defendant that the suit land originally belonged to Sur Ali and others and RS Khatian was prepared in their names. On the acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government, they became tenants under the Government and MRR Khatian was correctly prepared in their names. For arrear of rents due to the Government with respect to the suit land, Certificate Case No.7402 of 1959-60 was started against the recorded owners of MRR Khatian and the land was put to auction and one Mir Ahmed auction purchased the suit land and got actual physical possession on 7-11-1962 through a Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1962-63 and possessed the land on payment of rents to the Government. The auction purchase Mir Ahmed transferred the auction purchased land to one Khatun and the said Khatun also exercised acts of possession over the suit land and on her death, the same was inherited by the defendant Nos. 1-4 and Mohammad Hussain, Shafiqur Rahman and Azizur Rahman. Mohammad Hussain, Shafiqur Rahman and Azizur Rahman transferred land of their share in favour of defendant Nos. 5-7 by four registered sale deeds on different dates the defendants encircled their purchased land with boundaries made a Kuria on some portion of the land and exercised acts of possession over the rest land. The defendant Nos. 1-4 sold land of their share to one Noorjahan. 

 8. Further case of the defendants is that, the alleged kabala deeds of the plaintiffs got no legal existence and those are forged, created and collusive deeds. The plaintiff, on the basis of those forged kabala deeds, did never exercise any act of possession on the suit land. MRR Khatian had been prepared 22 years back but the plaintiff did never make any attempt to have the MRR Khatian corrected. The plaintiff did not put forward any claim within twelve (12) years of the date of auction purchase and also of taking of the delivery of possession on the auction purchased land by the auction purchaser and the plaintiff claim and the suit stood barred by limitation. The plaintiff got no cause of action to file the suit against the defendants. The suit as framed is also not maintainable. 

 10. The learned trial Judge held that it had been proved that Mir Ahmed purchased the land in auction and went into possession by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1962-63 and after that the defendants acquired title and possession over the suit land by virtue of sale deeds. The trial Judge further held that it had been proved that by the sale deeds, Exhibit-3 and 4, the plaintiffs did not get into possession over the suit land and the suit land by and the said deeds were not acted upon and by the auction sale, the title of the plaintiffs, if any, had been extinguished. The trial Judge held, further, that all the PWs admitted that the defendants possessed some portion of the suit land by encircling the same with fencing and that had been also proved by Exhibit-5, the Report of the Advocate Commissioner and some PWs admitted that the defendants were in possession over the entire suit land and the defendants grew ''pelong dal'' there. The trial judge came to the finding that MRR Khatian had been prepared long after the plaintiff obtained sale deeds but no attempt had been made by him to have the MRR Khatian, corrected. The trial judge found, further, that it was natural that the recorded owners of the suit land would be the certificate debtors. The trial judge found that the plaintiffs though were required to file suit for setting the sale did not do that. The trial judge, ultimately, expressed the view that the suit as framed was not maintainable and the same was barred by limitation. With the above findings, the trial judge negative the claim of the plaintiffs and dismissed the suit. 

 22. Plaintiff in paragraph No. 4 and 5 of the plaint pleaded that the defendants expressed that the suit land i.e., the land of RS Khatian, for arrears of rents, was sold in auction in 1960 and they purchased the land from the auction purchaser and in the event of disclosure of any Bainama (sale certificate) and Dakhalnama (Writ of delivery of possession), those will be regarded as illegal, ineffective and baseless and the said auction sale was not acted upon and the auction purchaser and his successors did not acquire any title. PW 1 in his evidence stated that the whole auction matter is absolutely false and the auction sale was not acted upon and the auction purchaser did not exercise any acts of possession over the auction purchased land. The defendant-petitioners in the written statement clearly stated that the suit land, for arrears of rents was put to auction in a Certificate Case No. 7402 of 1959-60 and one Mr Ahmed auction purchased the land and got actual physical possession on 7-11-1962 through Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1962-63 and possessed the land on payment of rents to the Government. It was further pleaded that the auction purchaser Mir Ahmed transferred auction purchased land to one Fatema Khatun and on the death of Fatema Khatun, her heirs being the owners of the land, transferred their share to the defendant Nos.5-7 and Noorjahan Evidence had been also led in support of the auction sale and possession of the defendants following auction purchase. Exhibit-Ka is the writ of delivery of possession in favour of the auction purchaser Mr Ahmed on 7-11-1972 in Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1962-63. The trial Court on consideration of the evidences and materials on record came to the finding that it has been proved that suit land was auction sold for arrear of rent due to the Government and it was the responsibility of the plaintiffs to file suit seeking relief against the auction sale which the plaintiffs did not do so. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it does not appear that the appellate Court below has adverted to this most important aspect of the case. It appears that the lower appellate Court has not addressed itself to the clear finding arrived at by the trial Court that it was the responsibility of the plaintiffs to seek relief against the auction sale. The appellate Court did not come to any positive finding whether the plaintiffs were required to seek relief against the auction sale. The Power appellate Court simply found that the decisions arrived at by the trial Court to the effect that the claim of the plaintiffs could not be eatertainable as because plaintiffs, on getting knowledge of the auction purchase, did not file any suit against the auction purchase, were not proper but it did not meet the positive finding arrived at by the trial Court that it was the responsibility of the plaintiffs to file suit against the auction sale. 

 24. Admittedly, Revisional Settlement (RS) Khatian had been prepared in the name of Sur Ali and others. The original plaintiff Eshaque Ahmed Sikder claimed to have purchased the suit land by way of two sale deeds registered on 5-2-1946 and 21-8-1952. Exhibits 3 and 4. MRR Khatian had been prepared long after the date of registration of the sale deeds of the plaintiffs. In the MRR Khatian, the name of the original plaintiff Eshaque Ahmed Sikder had not been recorded, rather the names of the RS recorded owners Sur Ali and others had been recorded in the Said MRR Khatian. The original plaintiff Eshaque Ahmed Sikder did not take any step to have the MRR Khatian corrected in his name. The trial Court found that the plaintiff did not make any attempt to have the record of right corrected in his name. The lower appellate Court also found that immediately after purchase, the plaintiff was required to get his name mutated in the connected record of right and due to non-recording of his name in the record of right, the certificate proceeding had been started. The certificate case had been started showing the recorded owners of the MRR Khatian as certificate debtors. The certificate officer was not supposed to know whether there had been any subsequent transfer from the recorded owners and whether the transferee was in possession on the suit land. So, it is natural that only those persons whose name had been recorded in the Khatian would be made parties i.e., certificate debtors in the certificate proceeding. The trial Court appears to have duly considered this aspect of the matter but the lower appellate Court misdirected itself in its approach on this aspect of the matter and the observation made by the lower appellate Court does not appear to be a proper and sound observation. 

 29. From the above, it appears that plaintiff''s suit was for possession and subsequent dispossession and the case was squarely covered by Article 142 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act. Now I am to refer to the relevant oral evidences on record to decide the factum of possession of the plaintiff and the defendants over the suit land. Plaintiff 1(ka) as PW 1 gave evidence for himself and for all the plaintiffs. He was aged about 30 years on 5-3-1986 when the evidence was recorded. This PW 1 stated that he did not file any case for setting aside the auction sale. He further stated that the rent receipts filed in the Court were subsequent to the filing of the suit. PW1 further gave evidence that defendant Nos. 5-7 forcible entered into the suit land and were in possession over some portion of the suit land. Again, he stated that on his prayer dated 6-5-1981, Advocate Commissioner was appointed and Advocate Commissioner reported that defendants were in possession over some portion of the land. PW1 did not state the date of dispossession from the suit land. PW 2 was aged about 35 years. In his evidence he stated that the defendants forcibly took over possession over 6/7 karas of land 4/5 years back. He could not say the Khatian and plot number of the suit land. This witness, further, stated that the defendants possessed land by erecting fencing. This witness further stated that he could not say on which date the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff. PW 3 gave evidence that the defendants, 4/5 years back, forcibly possessed about 8 karas of land. This witness again stated that the defendants erected house over the suit land 8/10 years back. PW 4 testified that 2-4 years back, the defendants forcibly possessed the entire suit land. PW 5 testified that the defendants, 3-4 years back, forcibly possessed some land. PW 6 testified that the defendants forcibly possessed 7/8 karas of land out of the suit land. PW 7, the learned Advocate Commissioner, gave evidence that he found a 'Kuria' over the suit land. 

 32. In RS Khatian No. 967 corresponding to MRR Khatian No. 9029, the plot No. being 4021, total land is 0.29 acres. Exhibit 3 is a Kabala deed dated 5-2-1946 executed by Musa Ali, Moklesur Rahman sons of Waziuddin, Mokbul Ali and Alimuddin sons of Sur Ali in favour of plaintiff Eshaque Ahmed transferring total 0.29 acre of land from the said plot and Khatian. Exhibit-4 is the Kabala deed dated 21-8-1952 registered by Suya Bibi and Anabibi other owners of the land, in favour of the said Eshaque Ahmed transferring 0.08 acre of land from the said plot Khatian No. Thus, the total land transferred came to 0.37 acres of land but there were only 0.29 acres of land in the said plot and Khatian. On scrutiny of the two Kabala deeds, Exhibit 3 and 4 it transpires that Exhibit-3 is only one page Kabala deed and Exhibit-4 is only one and a half page Kabala deed. MRR Khatian has been prepared long after the sale deeds of the plaintiffs and admittedly, the plaintiff did not make any step to have the MRR Khatian corrected. The trial Court, on a consideration of the two ''deeds Exhibits-3 and 4, the MRR Khatian, legal evidences and other materials on record came to the decision that the plaintiff, as a matter of fact, did not get into possession over the suit land and the said two sale deeds were not acted upon and the suit, having not been filed within the period of limitation prescribed by law, the same stood barred by limitation. The lower appellate Court does not appear to have reversed the said findings of the trial Court property. The appellate Court in a sweeping way without considering the legal evidences and other materials on record found that the cause of action had been proved and the suit had been filed within the period of dispossession. It needs be mentioned here that the trial Court on a proper discussion of the oral evidences of both the PWs and DWs came to a decision and dismissed the suit. It is surprising that the lower appellate Court in reversing the decision of the trial Court did not discuss the oral evidences of PWs and DWs which it was required to do being the last and final Court of fact. The appellate Court simply stated that the PW 1 admitted that the defendants prior to the institution of the suit forcibly possessed some portion of the suit land. The lower appellate Court was required to find on which date the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit land and whether the suit was filed within 12 years from the date of dispossession to get a decree for recovery of Khas possession. My considered view is this that the question of limitation had not been properly treated by the lower appellate Court. 

 36. Admittedly, MRR Khatian had been prepared long after the alleged kabala deeds of the plaintiffs and MRR Khatian stands in the name of the original owners Sur Ali and others. The MRR Khatian got a presumption of possession, at least, at the time when the same had been prepared and the correctness of the presumption of possession did not appear to have been rebutted by the plaintiff's side.

Mahmud Hasan Chowdhury and others ……… petitioners

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-8 to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 9-7-2019 passed by the learned Judge (Joint District and Sessions Judge) of Land Survey Tribunal, Khulna in Suit No. Land 580 of 2014 rejecting an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 read with section 145A/145D of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for rejection of plaint should not be set-aside and/or such other or further or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts in short are that the opposite party Nos. 1-8 as plaintiffs filed Land Tribunal Suit No.580 of 2014 under section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for correction of record-of-right against the petitioners and opposite party Nos.9-11 who were defendants. 

 3. In above suit defendants filed a petition under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure, 1908 for rejection of plaint. It was alleged that before the establishment of Land Survey Tribunal plaintiff filed Title Suit No.1105 of 2008 for the self same property praying and for same relief in which defendants are party and above suit is pending for trial in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Khulna. In violation of Section 145(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 plaintiffs have filed this second suit for the same property so the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 6. Mr Md Mamun Aleem, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the opposite parties filed a suit for correction of record-of-rights before establishment of the Land Survey Tribunal that suit could be brought to the tribunal under section 145A(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. A new and second suit for the same cause was barred by law. 

 10. At the outset it is to be mentioned that Chapter XVIIA of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 was introduced in the above Act by Act No. IX of 2004 for establishment of land Survey Tribunal for entertaining only the suits arising out of final publication of the last revised record-of-rights. In 2004 the last revised record-of-right was the Bangladesh survey or BS khatian. The land survey tribunal has been vested with jurisdiction to determine the correction or falsity of BS khatians. The tribunal has no jurisdiction to determine or declare right to property or right to office which a Civil Court has.

lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General with Md Abdul Hai, DAG and Md Shahidul Islam Khan, AAG and Syeda Rabia Begum, AAG -------- For the Petitioner. 
Mustafizur Rahman, Advocate -------- For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Assistant Horticulturist ------- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner
VS
MA Sattar Bhuiyan and others ---------- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioners No. 1(a)-1(f) one MA Sattar Bhuiyan as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 218 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for perpetual injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiff in owning and possessing the suit land and also from evicting the plaintiff therefrom, contending inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to one Kadam Mia, Kuran Mia, Nur Khatun, Abdul Malek, Asia Khatun and Amode Ali. One Mazaharul Hoque and others purchased the said land from them by a registered sub-kabala in the year 1965. Thereafter, Mazaharul Hoque and others mutated their names, and obtained separate khatian and used to possess the suit property by payment of rent to the government sheresta regularly. The RS khatian was accordingly prepared in the name of Mazaharul Hoque and others. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Mazaharul Hoque and others for demarcation of their purchased land filed an application before the then Circle Officer (Rev), Savar on the basis of which a demarcation Case being No. 21/1981-82 was started and upon field measurement the applicants got their purchased land demarcated with specific boundaries. Thereafter, Mazaharul Hoque and others transferred 3.51 acres of land by several transferred deeds in favour of the plaintiff and the number of transfer deeds were thirteen of the year 1990 and since then the plaintiff has possessed the suit property. After purchase, the plaintiff mutated his name in respect of his purchased land and paid rent regularly. The plaintiff has been possessing the suit property by plantation of various trees and growing crops therefrom. While the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the suit property peacefully, the defendant No.1 to the original suit demanded bribe from the plaintiff on different pretext and being refused, the defendant No. 1 threatened the plaintiff with the help of some riotous people. On 25-6-1991 the defendant No.1 along with some terrorist resisted the work of the plaintiff's people on the suit property and they damaged some tree and tried to evict the plaintiff from the said land which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for permanent injunction. 

 7. The learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-petitioner submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Attorney-General further submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned courts below is perverse in the eye of law, which is based on misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Deputy Attorney-General (herein after DAG) in his submission submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court were totally misconceived in ignoring that the disputed property is out and out an abandoned property and the government by operation of law has been enlisted the property as abandoned in the year 1972 when the original owners who were non-Bengali people in origin/nationality migrated to Pakistan leaving behind this country, the People's Republic of Bangladesh after its independence. The learned DAG also submits that the papers produced from the side of the plaintiffs are collusive, forged and were not acted upon and that the learned courts below failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law and factual aspects of the case and there has been total non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. That the suit properties is under exclusive possession and control of the government and the government by the concerned Agriculture Department is owning and possessing the suit property which is commonly known as "Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Base". The learned DAG after producing some official documents through supplementary affidavit submits that some important information supported by official papers which are very much essential for disposal of the matter, has been dropped out at the time of filing of the civil revision, which is unintentional and beyond the knowledge of the concerned persons who placed the matter in favour of the petitioners. The learned DAG with regard to this argued that, for proper adjudication into the matter-in-dispute and for ends of justice; all these papers and official documents are very much necessary for consideration of this Court to arrive at a correct decision as to the matter of adjudication between the parties. With regard to this, the learned DAG argued that the property-in-dispute is absolutely an abandoned property and admitting that fact the plaintiff applied before the Secretary concerned of the government for releasing the suit property from the abandoned property's list on 12-11-1990 which has already been exhibited as Exhibit-'Gha' as per Abandoned Property Case No. 02 of 1972 and concerned file which has been lying with the Anti-corruption Department in connection with Kotwali Police Station Case No. 6(3) 87 and that was earlier ceased and the defendant's witness No. 1 in his deposition has mentioned about this. The photocopy of that document (official) was not considered by the trial court, and the same has been kept with the record. The learned DAG argued that after promulgation of the President's Order No. 16/1972, the suit property has been vested in the government under the Abandoned Property (land building and any other property) Rules, 1972 vide Notification dated 8-5-1972 and after that, the concerned Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar (North), Dhaka by his office Memo No. 2404(4) Rev/73 dated 19-5-1973 issued a letter to the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar, Dhaka for handing over charge of the abandoned property of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery at Savar. The photocopy of the aforesaid memo has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner marked as Annexure-'A'. The learned DAG also submits that the concerned Circle Officer (Rev), Savar by his office Memo No. 823/2 dated 30-5-1973 issued a letter to the Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, (North), Dhaka regarding handing over the possession of "Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery, Savar and its photocopy has been marked as Annexure-'B', and earlier to that, the District Agricultural Officer vide his office Memo No. 912/1(5) dated 11-4-1973 issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for handing over the charge of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery and the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar also issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner vide his office Memo No. 409/1(6)-SA dated 19-4-1973 for handing over the possession of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery of Savar and the Photostat copy of the aforesaid letters are marked herewith as Annexure-'C' and 'C-1'. Another letter relating to the handing over of possession issued by the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar vide Memo No. 696/1(3)-SA dated 16.05.1973 in favour of Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (north), Dhaka is also annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'D'. The learned DAG during his submission also submits that the all papers relating to mutations of the plaintiff including the DCR and other rent receipts in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party has been cancelled by the concerned authority viz. AC (land) Savar vide his office Memo No. 86 dated 19-2-1998 and there is no record yet has been prepared in favour of the plaintiff and the earlier office order vide Memo No. 86 dated 19-2-1998 is in force till today vide Annexure-'E' and during the present settlement operation the connected B.S. record of the disputed land has been prepared in the name of the government and that record is still in existence. The leaned DAG further submits that, all these papers go to show that the government is possessing the disputed property and the copies of the connected BS khatians are annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'F' series and the suit property was duly handed over by the connected Tahsildar, Bagdunia Tahshil Office, Savar preparing the lists of articles in favour of the agriculture department, Ministry of Agriculture and the lists of articles are also annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'G' series and in this way the government is possessing the suit property through Agriculture Department as abandoned property and the Agriculture Department paid the lease money to the government by taking the DCR. The photocopies of the DCRs showing payment of lease money has been marked as Annexure-'H' series. The learned DAG also submits that the vendors of the plaintiff-opposite party were not the Bangladeshi nationals and, as such, they had no legal right to enter into any agreement, sale or execution of a document of transfer in favour of the plaintiff or his predecessor-vendors. The list of abandoned property has been marked as Annexure-'I'. The learned DAG argued that the vendors of the deeds in favour of the plaintiff since were not Bangladeshi citizens, their whereabouts are not known after the war of liberation in the year 1971, and after independence of Bangladesh their names are not included in the voter lists. In support of the aforesaid contention the learned DAG has pointed out the voter lists of the year 1976 which is marked as Annexure-'J'. The learned DAG lastly submits that, all these papers which are purely official makes it clear that the title documents in favour of the plaintiff as alleged are all created spurious papers which have got no legal effect or force to substantiate the prima-facie title and possession of the plaintiff and the so called clearance certificate issued by the Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, Dhaka in favour of the plaintiff is also a created spurious paper which is forged and not acted upon, inasmuch as; at the relevant time under the government of Bangladesh there was no such officer/office in the name of Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, Dhaka. The learned Deputy Attorney-General with regard to this, has drawn my attention during his submission that under the District of Dhaka, from the official documents it is apparent that the office of the Concerned SDO was designated in the name of SDO, Sadar (North), Dhaka and in support of this; the learned DAG produce some corresponding letters and documents of the concerned office which has been marked as Annexure-'K'. In support of the contention given by the learned DAG, he has cited some decisions of our Apex Court and the learned Attorney-General with regard to the respective contention of the government and the grounds of the revisional application in his submission specifically argued that the suit as instituted by the plaintiff was not at all maintainable under the purview of section 54 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 since the plaintiff to the suit during trial has hopelessly failed to discharge his onus in proving that he has prima-facie title and exclusive possession in the disputed property, but the learned courts below totally overlooked the said legal aspect of the case and thereby committed gross illegality in deciding the merit of the suit as well as the appeal, which deserve interference of this Court. The learned Attorney-General further submits that the papers produced from the custody of the government inasmuch as; are all official documents; these have a presumption of correctness under the ambit of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 and the papers which has been submitted along with the supplementary affidavit requires consideration of this Court under the ambit of law as this Court is quite empowered to look into these papers which has falsified the pleading's case of the plaintiff and has enable the court to arrive at a correct decision. The leaned Attorney-General Mr Alom in this regard, has referred some decisions of our Apex Court and lastly submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during passing the judgment and decree since committed gross illegality and not evaluated the evidence on records in its true perspective and not considered the material facts, causing an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in the eye of law and, as such, the Rule has got every merit to succeed. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Attorney-General and the learned Deputy Attorney-General in support of the case of the government, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that, both the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or infirmity, rather; in deciding the fate of the plaintiff's case the courts below rightly assessed the evidence on record and also considered the factual aspects of the, case. The learned Advocate after submitting a counter affidavit on behalf of the opposite parties further submits that the plaintiff to the suit has successfully proved his case by adducing sufficient evidence that in the suit property the plaintiff have prima-facie title and exclusive possession, but the defendants having no manner of right, title, interest and possession therein, illegally threatened the possession of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below in their observation and findings rightly arrived at a decision that the property-in-dispute is not an abandoned property or the defendants have no authentic paper to substantiate their claim that the property is abandoned property, and scrutinizing the documentary as well as oral evidence, both the trial and appellate court below concurrently found that the present Opposite parties have title and exclusive possession in the suit land and accordingly decreed the suit and dismissed the appeal, both on contest, respectively. It is submitted by the learned counsel of the opposite parties that the suit property has never been included in the list of abandoned property or published in any official gazette and the petitioners as defendants could never produce any such document to support their claim and that the concerned authority did not serve any notice as per the requirement under Article 7 of the President's Order (PO) No. 16 of 1972 and never took possession of the suit land, which also depicts from the cross-examination of the Defendant's witnesses but the case of the plaintiff that the vendors of the plaintiff purchased the suit property from the S.A. recorded tenants Madan Mia, Kadam Mia and others (Exhibit-7 series) and accordingly they got delivery of possession, and their names were mutated and they paid rent, is proved and that the plaintiff could prove that the vendors of the plaintiff were the owners of the suit land in whose names RS Khatian No.10 and 104 Exibit-7(gha) and 7(umo) were prepared and that they never left this country for Pakistan and they got the suit land demarcated vide সীমানা নির্ধারণী কেইস নং-২১/১৯৮১-৮২ (Exhibit-5), filed in the office of the Revenue Officer, Savar, Dhaka and the Sub Divisional Officer, Dacca Sadar, Dacca vide Memo No. 39 VP Dated 11-1-1982 in reference to AP Clearance Case No. 1/82 (Savar) Issued a Clearance Certificate for mutation of name (Exhibit-8) and that the suit property had not been enlisted or leased out as abandoned property. The leaned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiff by 13 Kabala Deeds purchased the suit property in 1990 from the RS recorded tenants and accordingly got delivery of possession and also got his name mutated and paid rents (Exhibit-3 series) and when the Defendant No. 1, an officer attached to the Government Sobhanbag Horticulture Centre, Savar tried to extort some illegal gains dishonestly from the plaintiff and when the plaintiff refused to be blackmailed, he started creating impediments and hurdles in the way of the plaintiff's possession in the suit property by using the name of the office and that of the Government and ultimately, the plaintiff initially filed a criminal case followed by the instant Civil Suit in which both the courts below held that the cancellation of the mutation in the name if the plaintiff was illegal and during trial all the plaintiff's witnesses corroborated the plaintiff's possession in the suit land, whereas; the case of the defendants as made out in their written statement was proved to be contradictory to the depositions of their witnesses. The learned Advocate submits that the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiff during trial of the original suit successfully proved the case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff has title and interest including possession over the disputed property and all the witnesses are competent, trustworthy and reliable, and, as such, courts below rightly relied upon the testimonies of the witnesses as examined from the side of the plaintiff and on the contrary, the witnesses adduced from the side of the defendants to substantiate their case, were totally failed to falsify the case of the plaintiff and prove the case of them (defendants), which is considered rightly by the learned trial court as well as the appellate court and there is no illegality or infirmity including misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of the material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate in support of his contention has referred some decisions of our Apex Court and in his concluding argument submits that the concurrent findings and decisions of both the courts below since not based on any illegality or infirmity, there is no reason to discharge the Rule. 

 12. In this case; it is apparent from the face of the records that the documents/papers produced at present from the side of the petitioners are all coming from official custody. With regard to this, I may not be out of place to advert that under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 it is presumed that the official acts as it appears, have been regularly performed and the court may presume the existence of such documents/papers as submitted from the side of the government in support of their contention and that's why these papers are accepted. The court also presumes the existence of the facts which is supported by these official papers and it is likely to have happened, under the ambit of the relevant provision of law as cited from the side of the learned Deputy Attorney-General. [Ref. 3 DLR 337; PLD 949 Privy Council 31; and 28 DLR 991. Hence, I find that the official acts supported by the series of papers which have been marked as annexures, definitely have got a presumptive value of its correctness. The papers produced from the side of the petitioners go to show that the plaintiff's mutation including up-to-date payment of rents is no more in existence, in respect of the disputed property. The present khatian also stands recorded in the name of the government. 

 13. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records, I find that both the parties to the suit in order to establish their pleading's case have adduced witnesses. Among them, PW 1 is the plaintiff himself MA Sattar Bhuiyan. This witness in his testimony tried to depose in support of his pleading. At a stage of his deposition he has frankly conceded that on the basis of thirteen sub-kabala 'deeds he has acquired title and interest in the disputed property. The plaintiff has failed to state the CS khatian number of the disputed land and also failed specify the boundaries of the disputed property in his deposition. It is the contention of the plaintiff in his testimony that his property (suit land) is being managed by his caretaker who uses to reside therein in a dwelling hut, but in the plaint; there is no mention about the existence of dwelling but of his caretaker. As to the cause of action of the suit, on perusal of the plaint I find that, it is also not mentioned in the plaint that in what date and time the defendant No. 2 and 3 threatened the plaintiff or his caretaker to dispossess from the disputed property. PW 1 has admitted at a state of his testimony that his mutation has been cancelled by the authority and he filed an appeal before the Divisional Commissioner. The plaintiff as PW 1 also testified that he does not know as to whether the Anticorruption Department has started a case against the concerned Circle Officer (Rev) and Tahashilder. In a reply to a question from the side of the defendants PW 1, the plaintiff admits at a stage of his testimony that he could not file any rent receipt showing his payment of rent for the disputed property after the year 1990 AD. 

 18. During cross-examination PW 4 testified at a stage that he is a businessman and a man of Kishoreganj. He resides in the land of former witness Nurul Islam (PW 3). During cross-examination in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants, PW 4 testified at a stage that he cannot say the name of mouza, khatian number and plot number of the suit property. 

 23. The last witness of the plaintiff is P.W.7 Haji Zahurul Islam, who has claimed himself another possession witness of the plaintiff. This PW 7 in his deposition at a stage testified that he knows the plaintiff and the suit land. This witness also testified in his testimony that from 1969 to 1990 AD, the suit property was possessed by the 'non-Bengali people' and from 1990 the plaintiff Abdus Sattar uses to look after the suit property. During cross-examination this witness with regard to the identity of the suit land testified that he cannot say the khatian number of the suit property and also cannot say about the cause of action of the suit and against whom the plaintiff instituted the suit. 

 28. Evaluating the testimonies of the witnesses along with other evidence led from the sides of the respective parties it transpires that the Plaintiff's witnesses who were examined from the side of the plaintiff are not independent, disinterested, and credible and none of the boundary men, as stated by the witness No. 3 of the plaintiff is examined to corroborate the pleading's case of the plaintiff as to his possession in the suit property. Apart from this, neither the four persons whose names is transpired from the deposition of PW 3 nor the so-called caretaker of the plaintiff who allegedly reside in the dwelling but of the suit property and who was allegedly taken away by the Police men has not been examined from the side of the plaintiff to substantiate his possession in the suit property, and cause of action of the suit. Accordingly, under the ambit of 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872 it is a legal presumption that had they been examined, they would not have supported the case of the plaintiff and as a result of that they have been withheld. [Ref. 10 DLR 447; 25 DLR 398; 22 DLR 431; 16 DLR 224; 30 DLR(AD)81; 31 DLR 405; 50 DLR 116 and 2 BLC (AD) 851. 

 32. It is a decided matter that, if the dispute involves complicated questions of title, the plaintiff must establish his title by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title. In this case the plaintiff assails the presumption of the Khatian, a kind of exercise the Court in a simple suit for permanent injunction should ordinarily avoid. [Ref. Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215). Apart from this, going through the evidence on records and the papers produced from the side of the government which have got a presumptive value of correctness it reveals that the case of the plaintiff with regard to the prima facie title and possession is not proved by any tangible, cogent and credible evidence, rather; the Plaintiff's witnesses contradicted the case of the plaintiff obviously in their testimonies and the Plaintiff's witnesses No. 02, 05, and 06 practically has admitted the case of the government.

lawyer:
Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record- For the Appellants. 
MA Quayum, Senior Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record-For Respondent Nos. 1-4. 
None Represented-For Respondent Nos. 5-7.
parties:
Karim Khan and others ----- Appellants
Vs
Kala Chand @ Chand Miah and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. Facts necessary for disposal of this appeal are that the appellants as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 16 of 1993 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rupganj, Narayangonj against the defendant-respondents for permanent injunction on the averments, inter alia, that Akbar Ali Bhuiyan was the owner of the land of CS Khatian No. 15 and some other lands and that Jonab Ali and others were the owners of the land of CS Khatian No. 243 and some other lands including the suit land. Prior to the CS operation, the land of CS plots of CS Khatian No. 15 was owned and possessed by Maizuddin and that at one time, he handed over possession of the land of the said khatian to Akbar Ali Bhuiyan. The lands of Khatian Nos. 15 and 243 were sold in auction and the landlord purchased the auction sold land of the said khatians. After the auction purchase, the auction purchased land including the suit land came in the hand of one Mohabbat Khan before 1940. Said Mohabbat Khan owned and possessed the suit land along with other lands on payment of rent to the Zamindar Mohabbat Khan died leaving behind sons: Ayer Khan, Taiub Khan and Ala Box and the SA and the RS records were prepared in their names. Ayer Khan died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs and they have been possessing the suit land by growing crops therein to the knowledge of all including the defendants. The defendants who have no right, title and interest as well as possession in the suit land tried to dispossess the plaintiffs on 19-3-1993, but due to the intervention of the people of the locality, they were not successful and in that back-ground, the plaintiffs were constrained to file the suit for the relief aforementioned. 

 3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 1-4 by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that Akbar Ali Bhuiyan was the owner and possessor of the land of CS Khatian No. 15 and Jonab Ali and others were the owners and possessors of the land of CS Khatian No. 243. The lands of the said khatians were sold in auction and Suja Khan, father of Mohabbat Khan and Immat Khan purchased the auction sold land from the Zaminder. Suja Khan died leaving behind sons: Mohabbat Khan and Immat Khan and the suit land fell in the saham of Immat Khan on amicable partition and as he was owning and possessing the same, RS record was prepared in his name and in the name of Mohabbat Khan. Immat Khan sold 45 decimals land out of 50 decimals land to defendant No. 1 (Kala Chand) from Plot No. 360 on 5-12-1977 and handed over possession thereof to him. Later one Immat Khan also sold 30 decimals land out of 36 decimals land from Plot No. 361 on 12-3-1979 to defendant No. 1 and handed over possession thereof to him. On 12-3-1979, Immat Khan gifted 4½ decimals land from Plot No. 360 to his two grand children: Serajul Islam Khan and Md Dulal Khan and handed over possession of the said land to them. On 12-3-1979, Immat Khan gifted 4 1/2 decimals land to his son, Md Rup Khan and handed over possession of the transferred land to him. The son, the grand children and the mother of the grand children of Immat Khan sold 1 decimal land from Plot No.360 and 6 decimals land from Plot No. 361 and some other lands to defendant No. 1 and handed over possession thereof to him. Defendant No.1 acquired 54 decimals land from Plot No.360 and 36 decimals land from Plot No. 361 and he got his name mutated on 3-3-1986 and has been paying rents to the Government and he has been possessing the lands for more than 13 years planting fruit trees. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land, but they filed the suit making false statements and, as such the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 9. So far as the trial Court is concerned, it appears that it did not consider the oral evidence on record in its entirety as to the possession of the suit land by the parties; it considered the evidence of the PWs and some of the DWs in a piece-meal manner and also failed to consider the presumption of the SA khatian and the rent receipts which were exhibited as exhibits-'4, '5' series and '6' series. The Appellate Court, the last court of fact, considered the evidence of both the PWs and the DWs and also the documentary evidence, namely: exhibits-'4, 5 series and 6 series' and came to the positive finding to the effect: 

 10. As noted in the leave granting order, in fact, the High Court Division interfered with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court on the view that "the plaintiffs did not mention the boundary of the specific plot and there is no specific demarcation, in that view of the matter granting injunction in favour of the plaintiff cannot be sustained." The High Court Division was totally wrong in taking the said view inasmuch as from the schedule to the plaint, it is prima facie clear that the plaintiff filed the suit for permanent injunction in respect of two plots being Plot Nos. 361 and 360, the total area of the land involved in the said two plots are 39+54 decimals respectively and the plaintiffs claimed the entire area of the said two plots. Therefore, it was not at all necessary for the plaintiff to give the boundary of the said two plots. In this regard, the learned Judge of the Single Bench totally misconceived the provisions of Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) inasmuch as the said provisions of the Code has clearly spelt out that where the subject-matter of the suit is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description of the property sufficient to identify it, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement of survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers. In the instant case from the schedule to the plaint, it is clear that the plaintiff mentioned the number of the CS and the SA Khatians and also the plot numbers of the lands in the suit and thus there was full compliance with the provisions of Order VII, rule 3 of the Code. And since no fraction or portion of the lands of the two plots was claimed, there was no necessity of giving any chauhaddi or boundary of the suit plots. Therefore, we find substance in the first submission as noted in the leave granting order.
